chunk_findings.detail: The subagent classification uses `sub = "subagents" in p.parts[len(root.parts):]`, which is wrong when the project directory is passed as `.`. `Path(".").parts` is `(".",)`, but `Path(".").rglob("*.jsonl")` yields paths such as `subagents/a.jsonl` whose `parts` are `("subagents", "a.jsonl")`; the slice `[1:]` therefore drops the `subagents` component and treats every subagent transcript as lead. For example, running `python3 -I scripts/token_report.py .` on a directory containing only `./subagents/a.jsonl` with one assistant call reports `subagents.calls == 0`, `lead.calls == 1`, empty `top_agents`, and subagent content in the lead carry aggregate, directly corrupting the lead-vs-subagent split.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/token_report.py:build_report

chunk_findings.detail: The lead `UNAVAILABLE` logic inspects `rep["unavailable"]` strings as if they were paths, but `read_entries()` raises `Unavailable(f"{path.stem}: ...")`, so unavailable entries are only file stems, not paths containing `subagents/`. Given a project directory with no lead transcript, one readable subagent transcript, and one unreadable subagent transcript such as `subagents/b.jsonl` with mode `000`, `lead_ok` remains false and `Path("b: PermissionError").parts` does not contain `subagents`; the code then sets `rep["lead"]["status"] = "UNAVAILABLE"`. The lead aggregate is marked unavailable because a subagent file was unreadable, not because a lead file was unreadable.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/token_report.py:build_report

chunk_findings.detail: `rewrites` is populated by `_fold_calls()` for both lead and subagent files, but `share_of_subagent_units` divides each class’s rewrite units by `rep["subagents"]["units"]`. This makes lead-only rewrites appear as a share of subagent units. For example, if a lead transcript has one gap rewrite worth 75,000 weighted units and subagents total 100 weighted units, the report prints `share_of_subagent_units` as `75000.0%` for that preceding-tool class, even though the rewrite came from the lead and is not a share of subagent spend.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/token_report.py:_finish_rewrites

chunk_findings.detail: The test is supposed to enforce “no transcript text, redacted,” but it only checks a few exact substrings. The fixture also contains the short tool-result string `"ok"` (and any 1–3 character prefix of the 400-character `"x"*400` result). If `build_report` or `render_text` leaked that text—for example by returning `{"note": "ok"}` or `{"preview": "xxx"}`—the test would still pass because neither `"ok"` nor `"xxx"` is asserted absent, so the redaction guard can be wrong.
